clue.text: Clothe her as Lear changing for full-scale practice

parts.note: to clothe someone is to dress them

indicators.note: the words her as Lear are changing, so their letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An actor must put the costume on her as King Lear for the final run-through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothe' looks like part of the anagram fodder but gives its synonym; only 'her as Lear' is jumbled by 'changing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A final run-through in costume is the complete, full-scale practice before opening night.

clue.text: Reposition back on field

parts.note: the rear is the back of something
a range is a field or extent, as in a range of options

explanation.surface: An instruction to move something back onto the field of play.
explanation.definitionFit: To reposition things is to put them in a new order or place, the same as reorganising them.

clue.text: Bismuth has lifted Indian chap

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters of bismuth's symbol and has are read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: Bi is the chemical symbol for bismuth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man in India has picked up some bismuth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns BIHAS upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sahib was the respectful form of address for a man, especially a European, in colonial India.

clue.text: Cheer her madly about century -it's rare

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, i.e. around, the abbreviation for century
the letters of cheer her are jumbled madly into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A crowd wildly cheers a woman celebrating a hundred, which is quite rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges CHEERHER to RECHERHE, and 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherche describes something exquisite and uncommon, choice and hard to find.

clue.text: Composer has time after holidays

indicators.note: after places the time letter behind the word for holidays

parts.note: hols is British slang for holidays

explanation.surface: A musician who writes music gets some time off after the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was an English writer of music, best known for The Planets suite.

clue.text: But area rearranged includes one rock garden plant

indicators.note: the jumbled letters include, i.e. hold within them, the numeral for one
the letters of but area are rearranged into a different order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, which as printed lacks one of the two I's the answer needs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gardener redesigns a patch of ground, adding a single alpine plant.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'rearranged' turns BUTAREA round and 'includes' adds I, giving the variant spelling AUBRETIA; the grid's AUBRIETIA needs a second I the clue never supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubrietia is a trailing purple-flowered perennial, a favourite in rockeries and on walls.

clue.text: Refurbish a Korean outfit, including military headdress

indicators.note: the words refurbish a Korean outfit are including, i.e. holding within them, the answer as a run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone renovates the uniform of a Korean unit, hat and all.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'refurbiSH A KOrean'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical peaked cap with a plume, worn by soldiers in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Boy is on top of team where it's sheltered

indicators.note: in a down entry, the boy's name is on top of, i.e. placed above, the word for team

parts.note: Lee is a boy's name
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A boy sits on the shoulders of his teammates in a sheltered spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee side of a ship or hill is the side away from the wind, so protected.

clue.text: Small and a large shoe

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A shop stocks footwear in both small and large sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is an open shoe held on by straps.

clue.text: A party to astound

parts.note: taken as written
a bash is an informal party

explanation.surface: Someone throws a party designed to amaze the guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to disconcert or take aback, close to leaving someone astonished.

clue.text: Famous person has fee to rejoice in

parts.note: a celeb is a celebrity, a famous person
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A star has been paid an appearance fee to enjoy herself at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To celebrate an event is to mark it joyfully, taking delight in it.

clue.text: Long-lasting rule; bad arrangement

indicators.note: a new arrangement of the letters of rule and bad is called for

explanation.surface: A long-standing regulation is described as a poor arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like part of the anagram signal but is fodder; 'arrangement' rearranges RULEBAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something durable lasts a long time without wearing out.

clue.text: Stumble on oil all over the place in Libya

parts.note: to trip is to stumble

indicators.note: the letters of oil are all over, scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone slips on oil spilled everywhere somewhere in Libya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' is the anagram signal, so 'the place in Libya' is left to define the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: Fabric on line is new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The washing hanging on the line is brand new.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is cloth woven from flax.

clue.text: Funny thing: one in suit in disco

indicators.note: funny suggests the letters of thing are behaving oddly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a club is one card in the suit of clubs

explanation.surface: Someone wears an amusing outfit to a dance venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges THING into NIGHT; a club is one card of a suit, the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a venue for dancing to recorded music, much like a dance club open late.

clue.text: He painted a policeman

explanation.surface: An artist moonlights as an officer of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English landscape painter; a constable is also the lowest-ranking police officer in Britain.

clue.text: Old one's birthday in the ten organised

indicators.note: the letters of in the ten are organised, i.e. put into a new order

parts.note: the printed fodder, which supplies eight of the nine letters; the setter evidently counted the I of one in it too

explanation.surface: An elderly person's birthday party is held in the evening, with ten organisers.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the fodder IN THE TEN is one I short of the answer; the setter seems to have meant 'one' to give I as well as define.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninetieth birthday is one reached only in old age, at ninety years.

clue.text: Support wise man taking time in part of theatre

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: the word for wise man is taking, i.e. holding inside, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A wise old patron supports the theatre, taking his time.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage is the area behind the stage, out of the audience's view.

clue.text: Tree that's always fresh

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
green means fresh or new, as in green shoots

explanation.surface: A tree that never seems to go stale.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen is a tree, such as a pine, that keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Beginner in hospital department ran on time

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newcomer in a hospital ward kept working through his shift.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone newly joining a profession or contest, a newcomer.

clue.text: Highlander behind a horse-racing venue

indicators.note: behind places the word for Highlander after the letter a

parts.note: a Highlander is a person from the Scottish Highlands, so a Scot

explanation.surface: A Scotsman trails behind at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Highlander is also the setter's pseudonym, adding a wink. ASCOT is a famous English racecourse near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the Berkshire racecourse, home of the Royal Ascot meeting.

clue.text: Garden tool beginning to rust in bathroom item

indicators.note: in places that first letter inside the word for a bathroom item

parts.note: a towel is an item found in a bathroom

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of rust

explanation.surface: A garden tool starts to rust after being left in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool with a scoop-shaped blade, used for digging in gardens.

clue.text: I wager Brown is outside; he's from Lhasa

indicators.note: the word for brown is outside, i.e. wraps around, the other letters

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
taken as written
to bet is to wager

explanation.surface: Someone bets that a man named Brown is outside, and that he comes from Lhasa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname but is the colour TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, so a person from there is a native of Tibet.

clue.text: Well done! Underwear very original initially

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of original

explanation.surface: Praise for a very original piece of lingerie design.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is a cry of approval meaning excellently done.

clue.text: The head meets the French aristocrat

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The headmaster meets a French nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble is a member of the aristocracy, such as a lord.

clue.text: BAA cost outrageous? Sauce!

indicators.note: the letters of baa cost are put outrageously into a new order

explanation.surface: A sheep complains that the price is outrageous, what cheek!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' also means cheek, which suits the outraged surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a brand of hot pepper condiment.

clue.text: Head beginning to organise party

parts.note: bean is informal slang for the head

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of organise

explanation.surface: A leader starts to plan a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A BEANO is British slang for a lively party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is an informal British word for a jolly celebration or knees-up.

clue.text: Girl, liable to change, but at hand

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name

indicators.note: the letters of liable are to change, i.e. be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl who tends to be fickle is nonetheless always around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' is the anagram signal on 'liable'; 'but' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available is ready and accessible, close by for use.

clue.text: Proverb: publicity takes time

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a piece of publicity
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Getting your name known takes a long while, as the saying goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional saying expressing a common truth.

clue.text: Problem solver has difficulties with nose

parts.note: troubles are difficulties
hooter is British slang for the nose

explanation.surface: A fixer struggles with a blocked nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubleshooter is someone employed to find and fix faults or disputes.
